strengths: Targeting instance-level, simulation-ready 3D tabletop scenes is highly relevant and timely for embodied AI and robotic manipulation policy learning.

The decoupled pose and scale alignment strategy is well-designed: using a Differentiable Rotation Optimizer (DRO) with a tri-modal loss (silhouette, edge Chamfer, and DINOv2 appearance) together with Top-view Spatial Alignment (TSA) and Ratio-Matched/Area-Weighted (RMA) scoring provides a robust way to overcome single-view scale/depth ambiguities.

Remarkable physical plausibility results: TabletopGen significantly reduces object collision rates (0.42% object-level collision compared to 8.23%–17.39% for existing baselines) and achieves high visual fidelity.

Extensive experimental validation, including standard visual/perceptual metrics (LPIPS, DINOv2, CLIP), physical collision rates, GPT-4o automated evaluation, a user study with 128 participants, component ablations, and physical interaction demos in Isaac Sim.
The paper is clearly written, and the supplementary material provides thorough implementation details, intermediate step visualizations, prompts, and runtime breakdown.
weaknesses: High computational latency: Processing a single scene with 9 objects takes approximately 32 minutes on an NVIDIA RTX 4090. The reliance on sequential calls across multiple heavy foundation models (ChatGPT, GroundedSAM-v2, Seedream, Hunyuan3D-3.0, and PyTorch3D) limits throughput and real-time utility.

Potential cascading errors from top-view generative hallucination: TSA relies on Seedream synthesizing an orthographic top-down view. 2D diffusion models often struggle with strict spatial/geometric consistency across novel viewpoints, which can lead to hallucinated or misplaced instances that RMA-scoring can only partially alleviate.

Lack of 3D metric evaluation against ground-truth 3D layouts: Quantitative evaluation is performed on 78 synthesized/in-the-wild images using 2D reprojection metrics, collision rates, and perceptual scores. Testing on an existing 3D dataset with ground-truth 3D bounding boxes/poses (or simulated ground truth) would provide direct quantitative validation of the 3D translation, rotation, and metric scale accuracy.

strengths: Addresses an important and timely task for embodied AI: creating simulation-ready, instance-level, collision-free 3D tabletop scenes for robotic manipulation, where dense layouts and fine spatial relationships are crucial.

The two-stage pose and scale alignment strategy is technically well-motivated: using a Differentiable Rotation Optimizer (DRO) with a tri-modal loss (silhouette, contour Chamfer, and DINOv2 appearance) combined with Top-view Spatial Alignment (TSA) effectively alleviates single-view depth and scale ambiguities.
Impressive collision-rate reduction compared to existing generative/compositional baselines (scene collision rate drops from 67–98% in baselines to 7.69%, and object pair collision rate to 0.42%).

Comprehensive empirical validation, including quantitative visual metrics, physics-based metrics, an extensive 128-participant user study, and demonstrations of modular scene editing and robotic pick-and-place execution in Isaac Sim.
weaknesses: High computational cost and latency: Generating a single scene with ~9 objects takes approximately 32 minutes on an RTX 4090 GPU, which could limit large-scale automated data generation pipelines without significant engineering optimizations.

Heavy reliance on proprietary/external multi-modal models: The pipeline chains multiple distinct components (ChatGPT, Seedream, GroundedSAM-v2, Hunyuan3D-3.0). Reliance on closed/proprietary models such as Seedream may pose reproducibility challenges.

Potential failure modes in top-view generative hallucination: Synthesizing an accurate top-down orthographic view from a single perspective image using a generative model is ill-posed and can hallucinate, omit, or distort heavily occluded or small objects in densely cluttered scenarios.

Lack of evaluation against ground-truth 3D geometry: The quantitative evaluation primarily relies on 2D render metrics (LPIPS, CLIP, DINOv2), GPT-4o scoring, and collision checks; evaluating against ground-truth 3D scans/layouts (e.g., on existing tabletop datasets like TO-Scene) for 3D bounding box and pose estimation accuracy would further strengthen the claims.

strengths: Clear task formulation and practical relevance: The paper focuses on tabletop scene generation tailored for embodied AI and robotic manipulation ('the last meter'), addressing clear limitations of room-scale scene synthesizers and asset-retrieval methods.

Effective two-stage spatial alignment design: Decoupling rotation estimation via differentiable rendering (DRO with a tri-modal loss) from translation/scale estimation via top-view synthesis and anchor scoring (TSA / RMA-Score) provides an effective heuristic to resolve single-view depth and scale ambiguities.

Strong physical plausibility and low collision rates: The method demonstrates a notable drop in object- and scene-level collision rates (Col_S down to 7.69% compared to baselines exceeding 67%), making the outputs directly usable in physics simulators such as Isaac Sim.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The authors conduct quantitative visual/perceptual comparisons, GPT-4o rankings, collision evaluations, a 126-participant user study, and robotic manipulation demonstrations in Isaac Sim.
weaknesses: High computational latency: Processing a single tabletop scene with 9 objects takes approximately 32 minutes on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU (Section 6.2). The heavy reliance on per-instance image-to-3D diffusion (~830s) and multi-step gradient descent rendering in DRO (~810s) significantly limits its practical throughput for large-scale synthetic data generation pipelines.

Heuristic pipeline of disparate foundation models: The framework relies heavily on chaining multiple commercial or pre-trained models (ChatGPT, Seedream, GroundedSAM-2, Hunyuan3D-3.0). It behaves predominantly as an automated workflow/scaffolding rather than introducing a unified, learnable 3D architecture, raising concerns regarding cross-component error propagation.

Potential inconsistency in generative top-view synthesis: The TSA stage relies on prompting an image generator (Seedream) to synthesize an orthogonal top view from the perspective reference image. 2D diffusion models are prone to hallucinating, omitting, or shifting relative positions of small tabletop items across disparate views, which may destabilize translation/scale inference in denser or more cluttered environments.

Simplified pose assumptions: The rotation recovery in DRO assumes rotation is constrained primarily to 1D yaw around the tabletop vertical axis after canonical upright correction. This assumption breaks down for objects placed at arbitrary 3D angles, tilted items, or complex tumbled configurations (e.g., pens resting diagonally against cups or leaning books).

Evaluation on non-ground-truth metrics: Because test scenes are generated from open-vocabulary text prompts or single images without paired ground-truth 3D meshes, evaluations rely heavily on 2D camera sweep metrics (LPIPS/DINO/CLIP best views) and LLM-as-a-judge (GPT-4o), which can carry inherent perceptual biases.

strengths: Clear motivation and practical focus: The paper targets the critical gap between 3D scene generation and physical simulation usability for embodied robotics, focusing on tabletop scenes where existing methods suffer from severe collision and floating artifacts.

Effective decoupled alignment pipeline: The decomposition into generative instance extraction, Differentiable Rotation Optimization (DRO with a tri-modal loss combining silhouette, Chamfer edge distance, and DINOv2 features), and Top-View Spatial Alignment (TSA via synthesized orthographic top-down views and RMA-score anchor selection) is technically sound and effective at resolving spatial conflicts.

Significant improvements in physical plausibility: Quantitative results demonstrate drastic reductions in collision rate (Col_S drops to 7.69% compared to 67–98% for baselines) and high dynamic settling stability (92.13% vs <10% for baselines).

Thorough evaluation and real-world robotic deployment: Beyond standard vision metrics and a 128-participant user study, the authors validate the synthesized data via zero-shot real-to-sim-to-real policy transfer on an AgileX PiPER robotic arm across three manipulation tasks without real-world fine-tuning.

High clarity and reproducible details: The paper provides clear explanations of the methodology, loss formulations, prompt templates, and camera sweep protocols in both the main text and supplementary material.
weaknesses: Multi-stage pipeline complexity and dependency: The framework chains multiple generative and foundation models (ChatGPT, GroundedSAM-v2, Seedream, Hunyuan3D-3.0). Errors or hallucinations at early stages (e.g., inaccurate instance segmentation or flawed top-view redrawing) could propagate through the pipeline without an explicit global verification or recovery mechanism.

Lack of inference time and computational cost analysis: Generating 3D meshes per instance, running image diffusion completion and top-view generation, and optimizing rotations via differentiable rendering with multi-start Adam for each object is likely computationally demanding. Reporting per-scene wall-clock runtime breakdown would clarify practical scalability.

Top-view synthesis fidelity: Relying on a 2D generative model (Seedream) to generate an orthographic top-down view from an arbitrary perspective image can be prone to perspective distortion or hallucination of occluded areas. A deeper discussion or ablation on failure modes of this generative top-view prior would strengthen the analysis.

Limited physical property estimation: Physical parameters like mass, center of mass, and friction coefficients appear to be set heuristically or via uniform defaults. While sufficient for basic pick-and-place, this limits performance in contact-rich or dynamic manipulation scenarios (as reflected by the lower success rate in block stacking).

strengths: Addresses an important and practical problem at the intersection of 3D vision and embodied AI: generating instance-separated, collision-free, simulation-ready 3D tabletop scenes for robotic manipulation data collection.

The decoupled layout alignment strategy is sensible and well-formulated: isolating yaw rotation optimization via differentiable rendering (with a tri-modal loss combining soft IoU, Chamfer edge, and DINOv2 features) and resolving metric scale/translation through synthesized top-down priors and an RMA-Score scaling anchor.

Thorough quantitative and qualitative evaluation against multiple recent baselines (ACDC, Gen3DSR, MIDI, MesaTask, SceneGen, FlashSculptor), demonstrating drastic reductions in collision rates (Col_O down to 0.42%) and strong physical stability (100% SS, 92.1% DSS).
A comprehensive human user study (126 participants) and ablations validate the visual and physical quality of the generated environments.

Strong system-level proof of concept via zero-shot real-to-sim-to-real policy learning: fine-tuning a π0.5 model entirely on synthetic demonstrations generated from a reconstructed tabletop photo and achieving high success rates on a physical robot arm.
weaknesses: The framework is a complex multi-stage pipeline that relies on several large external foundation models (ChatGPT/MLLM, GroundedSAM-2, Seedream, Hunyuan3D-3.0). Failure or hallucination in early stages (e.g., inaccurate segmentation, generative completion artifacts, or inconsistent top-view synthesis) can cascade through the downstream alignment.

The rotation parameterization is restricted to 1-DoF yaw rotation around the gravity axis, assuming all objects stand upright on the tabletop. While reasonable for standard tabletop setups, it cannot handle tilted, fallen, or non-upright objects.

Synthesizing an orthographic top-down view using a 2D diffusion model (Seedream) without explicit 3D conditioning can suffer from hallucinations, missed objects, or geometric discrepancies in cluttered or heavily occluded tabletop scenarios.

The paper lacks discussion on computation time and runtime costs required to generate an entire interactive scene from scratch (e.g., API calls, mesh reconstruction, and multi-hypothesis gradient descent in DRO).

strengths: Addresses an important and practical problem in embodied AI: generating interactive, physically plausible, simulation-ready 3D tabletop scenes from text or a single image to alleviate the data bottleneck in robot manipulation.

The decoupled pose and scale alignment strategy (DRO for yaw rotation optimization via a tri-modal loss, and TSA utilizing top-view generation, stacking priors, and RMA-Score anchor selection) effectively circumvents the depth distortion and collision issues common in single-view monocular back-projection.

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple axes: quantitative visual/perceptual metrics (LPIPS, DINOv2, CLIP), physical collision rates (Col_O, Col_S), physical stability metrics (Support Stability, Dynamic Settling Stability), multi-aspect GPT-4o evaluation, and a well-conducted human user study with 128 participants.

System-level real-to-sim-to-real demonstration on physical hardware: successfully deploying a pi0.5 policy trained solely on synthetic trajectories onto an AgileX PiPER robotic arm across three manipulation tasks confirms the downstream utility of the generated scenes.
weaknesses: Restricted rotation degrees of freedom: The framework constrains instance rotation to a 1-DoF yaw rotation around the world Z-axis under the assumption that all objects have been canonicalized upright. This assumption breaks down for scenes containing tilted, fallen, or resting non-upright objects (e.g., a tipped bowl, a tilted pen leaning against an object, or randomly oriented clutter).

Heavy multi-stage dependency on commercial/closed foundation models: The pipeline chains multiple disparate generative tools (ChatGPT, Seedream, GroundedSAM-2, Hunyuan3D). Failure or hallucination in intermediate steps—such as inaccuracies in the 2D top-view synthesis or flawed commonsense dimensions from LLM queries—can cascade, and the paper lacks an in-depth analysis of error propagation and pipeline failure modes.

Top-view consistency and occlusion: Synthesizing an orthographic top-down view from an arbitrary perspective image using a generic 2D generative model is inherently ill-posed and susceptible to view inconsistency, hallucinated object placements, or missed occluded instances.

Scope of real-robot evaluation: While the real-world policy transfer is an impressive addition, it is evaluated on a single physical tabletop setup across three pick-and-place/stacking variants; broader evaluation over more diverse real-world tabletop environments would further substantiate the claimed generality.
